missions.title: GapDB Control Journal Proving Ground
missions.outcome: Prove a narrow durable authority and recovery slice over a pinned gapdbd sidecar.
missions.primary_falsification_target: GapDB can atomically support the control journal, projection, checkpoint, restart epoch, and side-effect-free playback through the two-agent zombie scenario.
entry_evidence: GapDB source revision, gapdbd digest, client version, and protocol version are pinned.
The existing two-agent invariant and fault harness is available.
exit_evidence: Crash and ambiguous-response injection passes at every durable boundary.
Replacement authority receives a fresh workspace and replay produces the same canonical digest.
All external GapDB adoption scenarios pass and a human signs the exact adoption tuple.
missions.risk: A client-only integration may hide owner lifecycle, response ambiguity, or replay defects.
missions.rollback: Stop after the proving slice and retain the current runtime as historical evidence; do not begin M2.

missions.title: GapDB-Only Production Authority
missions.outcome: Move all authority capabilities to the event and CAS model and erase SQLite from the production graph.
missions.primary_falsification_target: Every authority capability can run without SQL constraints, dual truth, SQLite fallback, or loss of refusal semantics.
entry_evidence: M1 journal, checkpoint, epoch, sidecar, and adoption evidence is accepted.
The Phase 1-3 authority behavior inventory is frozen.
Consumer-owned persistence port contracts are identified.
exit_evidence: All authority ports and applicable scenario, race, fault, and mutant suites pass on GapDB.
Recovery and ambiguous-response tests cover every authority-changing event family.
Source, module graph, SBOM, and binaries contain no SQLite production implementation.
non_goals: Silently import unsupported legacy SQLite state.
missions.risk: A table-shaped key translation could preserve accidental SQLite semantics and weaken atomicity.
missions.rollback: Revert the unshipped adapter branch as a unit; never ship dual writes or a fallback.

missions.title: Production Mission Execution and Beads Composition
missions.outcome: Compose real agent, workspace, tracker, review, and Git integration paths without losing concurrency safety.
missions.primary_falsification_target: The concurrency crown jewel survives when GapDB, Beads, Git, workspaces, processes, agents, and human edits disagree.
entry_evidence: A qualified Beads tuple and portable conformance contract are pinned.
Git, workspace, review, and integration product laws are frozen.
exit_evidence: Two real agents work concurrently in distinct lease-scoped workspaces.
Zombie, dishonest tracker, human reassignment, review-independence, and repository-fence scenarios pass.
Conflicts preserve candidates and create explicit repair work.
non_goals: Implement the neutral acceptance kernel or public API.
missions.risk: Production composition can accidentally grant authority through tracker, process, or filesystem state.
missions.rollback: Keep the qualified domain services and remove the unqualified production composition root.

missions.title: Stack-Neutral Acceptance Runtime
missions.outcome: Judge stack-neutral claims using explicitly bound, provenance-rich evidence providers.
missions.primary_falsification_target: One neutral gate can judge the same claim through materially different providers without importing ecosystem semantics.
entry_evidence: M2 durable event and evidence substrate is accepted.
Candidate, WorkRevision, review, and governance identities are stable.
The acceptance evidence contract is ratified.
exit_evidence: Different provider kinds prove one claim contract and yield the same decision.
Missing providers, stale evidence, waivers, and targeted invalidation behave explicitly.
Architecture mutants prove the acceptance kernel contains no ecosystem or provider imports.
non_goals: Make this repository's Go commands universal product law.
missions.risk: Convenient provider behavior could leak language or tool semantics back into the kernel.
missions.rollback: Disable unqualified provider bindings while retaining durable evidence as non-admissible history.

missions.title: Orchestrator API 2.0, Native Operations, Progress, and CLI
missions.outcome: Expose the complete production process through one typed application boundary and normal CLI.
missions.primary_falsification_target: A client can drive, disconnect from, resume, and understand a mission without reading Beads, Markdown, worktrees, Git refs, or GapDB directly.
entry_evidence: M2 authority, M3 production execution, and M4 acceptance are accepted.
API 2.0, progress, operation, and compatibility contracts are ratified.
exit_evidence: Black-box API and normal CLI complete equivalent missions.
Operations survive disconnect and restart; snapshot plus watch converges after resynchronization.
API 1.3 fixtures translate safely or return typed incompatibility.
non_goals: Implement MCP inside the core binary.
missions.risk: A transport-shaped API could recreate generic mutation or leak host authority.
missions.rollback: Retain internal application capabilities and remove unqualified public transports or compatibility mappings.

missions.title: Core Production Qualification and Release
missions.outcome: Qualify clean installation and sustained multi-mission operation as the core production release.
missions.primary_falsification_target: Independently proven components remain safe under sustained concurrency, arbitrary crash timing, installation, restart, and operator recovery.
entry_evidence: Signed GapDB and Beads production tuples are pinned.
Supported platform and load targets are ratified.
exit_evidence: Load, soak, crash, recovery, security, backup, and restore campaigns pass with exact census.
Installed core requires no Python, SQLite, or MCP.
Operators can diagnose every durable blocked state without editing GapDB directly.
non_goals: Delay the core release for the optional MCP adapter.
missions.risk: Correct components may fail at lifecycle, load, packaging, or operator-recovery seams.
missions.rollback: Withhold the release artifact and preserve source-bound qualification evidence for repair.

missions.title: Optional Stateless MCP 2026-07-28 Tasks Adapter
missions.outcome: Provide an independently packaged agent-native projection over API 2.0.
missions.primary_falsification_target: Connection loss, task expiry, input pauses, and cancellation races cannot alter or replace durable mission authority.
entry_evidence: M5 API 2.0 and native operations are accepted.
MCP 2026-07-28 core and Tasks extension revisions are pinned.
exit_evidence: The core builds and completes its workflow with the MCP module absent.
Stateless multi-instance, task-loss, input, cancellation-race, and progress-resume scenarios pass.
CLI-only and MCP-driven workflows produce equivalent terminal evidence.
non_goals: Create MCP-only workflow semantics or place MCP on the core release critical path.
missions.risk: Transport task identity or lifecycle could be mistaken for domain authority.
missions.rollback: Remove or disable the independent adapter without changing the core application or mission state.
